title: Key Vault Secrets, Keys, and Certificates
description: Dive into the three main object types in Key Vault and learn when to use each one.

data.text: Each object type in Key Vault serves a distinct purpose. Secrets store plain-text values. Keys perform cryptographic operations. Certificates are keys wrapped in a certificate lifecycle, including issuance and renewal.

cards.title: Secrets
cards.description: Opaque values up to 25 KB each. Best for API keys, connection strings, and passwords.
cons: Stored as plain text inside the vault

cards.title: Keys
cards.description: Cryptographic keys for encryption, decryption, and signing.

cards.title: Certificates
cards.description: TLS/SSL or code-signing certificates with auto-renewal.

data.title: Store and Retrieve a Secret
data.content: Add a connection string to Key Vault and read it back with the Azure CLI.
data.code:
# Store a secret
az keyvault secret set   --vault-name myKeyVault   --name "DefaultConnection"   --value "Server=tcp:my-sql.database.windows.net;..."

# Retrieve a secret
az keyvault secret show   --vault-name myKeyVault   --name "DefaultConnection"   --query value -o tsv

data.title: Create an RSA Key
data.content: Provision an RSA key for signing or encryption.
data.code: az keyvault key create   --vault-name myKeyVault   --name "my-signing-key"   --kty RSA   --size 2048   --ops sign verify encrypt decrypt

data.title: Work with Key Vault Objects
data.description: Create a Key Vault, store a secret, generate a key, and verify the objects exist.
steps: Set a secret named 'ApiKey' with value 'secret-123'.
List all secrets and keys to verify they exist.
data.expectedOutcome: You see the secret and key in the Key Vault and can retrieve their values.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use secrets for simple values like passwords and connection strings.
Use keys when you need encryption or signing.
Use certificates when you need TLS or auto-renewal.
data.takeaway: Key Vault is not just a safe for passwords — it is your app's cryptographic backbone.
